purpose: Hydroxychloroquine is used to treat autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, helping to reduce pain, swelling, and flares. It can also be used to prevent or treat malaria. Many people take it long-term to help keep their autoimmune disease under control.
how_it_works: This medicine works by calming down an overactive immune system that is mistakenly attacking your own body. It interferes with certain immune signals that cause inflammation and damage. Think of it like a volume dial that turns down the immune system's harmful activity without completely shutting it off.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, or diarrhea — especially when first starting. Some people notice headaches or dizziness. Skin may become more sensitive to sunlight, so wearing sunscreen is important. Rarely, it can cause changes in skin color or mild rashes.
warnings: The most important warning is that this medicine can rarely affect your vision over time by causing damage to the retina at the back of your eye. Because of this, you need a dilated eye exam before starting and every year while taking it. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any blurry vision or trouble seeing colors. Also let your doctor know if you have heart rhythm problems, liver or kidney disease, or a condition called G6PD deficiency, as this medicine may not be right for you.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for autoimmune conditions is 200 mg to 400 mg taken by mouth once daily or split into two doses. It is almost always taken with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will find the right dose based on your weight and condition. It may take several weeks to months before you feel the full benefits.
